newsitem.title: USA: Brazil's Malan plays down Mercosur single currency.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Malan plays down Mercosur single currency.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan on Tuesday played down the idea of creating a single currency for the Mercosur South American common market.

Malan told a news conference on the fringes of the IMF/World Bank spring meeting that his Argentine counterpart, Roque Fernandez, had talked about a single currency but "did not say that it would happen next week, or next year."
Fernandez, whose country has pegged the peso to the U.S. dollar since 1991 under a currency board system, mentioned the issue to reporters during a weekend visit to Rio de Janeiro.

Mercosur was set up in 1995 by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay to eliminate most trade barriers among their economies and to establish common external tariffs for imports from other countries.
They also have free trade agreements with Chile and Bolivia and have held talks to reach a similar deal with Venezuela.
Malan said setting up a single currency would be a very long-term proposal, reminding reporters that the European Union took decades to approach and agree on that issue.
"Some things in life take time. This is one of them," he argued. "This is not a matter for tomorrow's headlines."
